textbook:
Clean cutaway textbook illustration of ONE human Type IIx skeletal muscle fibre (fast glycolytic fibre), centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around the structures so labels can be attached later. The illustration's own neutral dark charcoal background must extend and touch all four edges of the canvas, filling it completely corner to corner. Do NOT draw any border line, rectangle outline, frame, mat, margin band, vignette or letterbox bar around the artwork, and do NOT draw the picture as a sheet or card lying on a surface.

HOUSE LOOK — match a refined educational plate exactly: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette of soft dusty tints (never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (never heavy black cartoon strokes), gentle soft shading with subtle dimensionality, and each structure its own distinct soft colour fill.

CRITICAL FRAMING FIX: the fibre's two ends must be CUT OFF by the canvas edges. Do NOT draw a rounded end cap, a full round cross-section disc, or any visible tip at either end of the fibre. The cylinder must run diagonally corner to corner and appear to CONTINUE beyond the frame in both directions, as if the picture were a cropped window onto the middle of a much longer object, like a sliced sausage seen through a rectangular hole, never a complete capsule floating with both ends visible inside the canvas. CRITICAL FRAMING CHECK: at BOTH ends, the fibre's own body colour must fully cover the picture right into the corner it exits through, touching BOTH edges that meet at that corner with no background-coloured triangle of empty space left over — imagine the square canvas was itself cut out of a much bigger picture of a long fibre, so the fibre's colour runs straight off two full edges (not just close to them) at each end. A flat cut face, a rounded tip, or ANY margin of background between the fibre and an edge at either end is a FAIL — verify mentally that the four corners are: fibre-colour, background, background, fibre-colour (diagonal composition) before finishing. MORPHOLOGY (the most important instruction): this is a single, long, UNBRANCHED, cylindrical fibre — a plain straight tube, wider than any single cell you would normally draw, running diagonally across the whole frame and cropped by the frame edge at BOTH ends so its true great length reads even though it cannot fully fit; it does not fork, branch, or taper into a Y anywhere. Its overall colour is a PALE PINK-CREAM (never deep red, never grey or colourless) because this is the lowest-myoglobin, most purely glycolytic of the three human fibre types, and it is visibly the WIDEST, most large-diameter fibre of its kind.

SURFACE AND INTERIOR:
- A thin teal-blue SARCOLEMMA outlines the whole cylinder.
- The fibre's surface carries two distinct patterns at once, both real and both must be visible together: (1) regular narrow dark dusty-rose and pale cream bands running ACROSS the fibre, perpendicular to its long axis, repeating evenly end to end like rungs on a ladder or the rings of a hose — a fine slate-blue Z-DISC line sits at the centre of every pale band, and this transverse banding runs the ENTIRE visible length with no gaps; (2) underneath that transverse banding, fine parallel MYOFIBRIL striping runs lengthwise along the fibre's long axis, giving the surface a combed, ribbed grain within each transverse band. Both patterns are visible at once — the transverse ladder-rung bands crossing the fibre, and the fine lengthwise myofibril grain inside each band — the way woven fabric shows both a weft and a warp.
- Along the fibre's outer rim, spaced out one after another, draw AT LEAST SEVEN separate oval, flattened, blue-violet NUCLEI, every single one tucked immediately under the sarcolemma at the periphery, oriented lengthwise with the fibre. Do NOT draw a single nucleus in the middle of the cell — that is wrong for this structure.
- In a neat long cutaway window along part of the fibre, reveal parallel MYOFIBRILS carrying the transverse striation pattern, with small amber-ochre MITOCHONDRIA scattered SPARSELY and INDIVIDUALLY between them (deliberately few and small — this is the low-mitochondria fibre, not a dense packed row), and abundant tiny round golden-tan GLYCOGEN GRANULE dots dusted liberally through the sarcoplasm between the myofibrils.
- Alongside the fibre, outside the sarcolemma, run one slender CAPILLARY (a thin tube with a fine crimson lumen) tracking the fibre's length — draw it clearly thinner and sparser than would be needed for a high-oxygen fibre.

DO NOT draw: a short stubby cell that fits entirely inside the frame; any branching, forking, or Y-shape; intercalated discs; a single central nucleus or any nucleus not touching the rim; dense red colouration; densely packed rows of large mitochondria; a smooth unstriated patch anywhere along the fibre; a cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, flagella or cilia. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars or watermarks anywhere in the image.
 The CAPILLARY must be rendered as a smooth, thin, continuously curving vessel of a single uniform dusty-rose/crimson tone throughout its length — like a fine blood vessel or thread. Do NOT render it as a candy-cane, barber-pole, segmented rod, swab stick, thermometer, or anything with alternating red-and-white stripes or beads; it must look organic and continuous, not like a manufactured object. Re-confirming: BOTH ends of the fibre must be sliced off by the picture edge — neither end may show a complete closed oval/round end-cap disc anywhere inside the canvas.

Photorealistic false-colour SCANNING ELECTRON MICROGRAPH of ONE human Type IIx skeletal muscle fibre (fast glycolytic fibre), centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous empty margin. Fill the whole square edge to edge with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox bar, and do not render the image as a plate lying on a surface.

The specimen is a long, thick, perfectly UNBRANCHED cylindrical fibre, resting on a subtly textured flat substrate, running diagonally across the frame and cropped by the frame edge at both ends so its great length reads clearly — it never forks or tapers into a Y, and it never sits as a short segment fully contained inside the frame. It is visibly the widest, largest-diameter fibre of its kind, with a smooth-surfaced but distinctly PALE PINK-CREAM false-colour tone (never deep red, never neutral grey) consistent with a low-myoglobin, fast glycolytic fibre.

Render true 3D surface relief: the surface carries many fine, closely-spaced ridges that encircle the fibre like the rings on a drinking straw or the rungs of a ladder laid crosswise over a rope — each ridge runs all the way around the tube's circumference, perpendicular to its long axis, giving the whole surface a corduroy-like cross-banded texture (the surface expression of the underlying sarcomere banding), and these encircling ridges repeat evenly, one after another, along the ENTIRE visible length with no smooth gaps. Along the fibre's flanks, spaced out one after another, show several long, shallow, oval BULGES in the surface, each one sitting exactly at the rim where an underlying peripheral nucleus pushes up against the sarcolemma from just inside — at least six or seven of them, spread along the length, never a single bulge in the middle. A slender neighbouring capillary vessel may lie alongside part of the fibre, partially in focus. Crisp fine surface texture, shallow depth of field so the far ends fall softly out of focus, cool studio microscopy lighting with a gentle rim light.

False-colour palette: pale dusty pink-cream fibre surface, a slightly cooler rose in the ridge grooves, on a neutral pale grey substrate and a dark uncluttered charcoal background.

DO NOT render: any branching or Y-fork; intercalated discs; a short stubby segment that fits entirely inside the frame; a smooth unribbed patch anywhere along the fibre; deep red or grey/colourless surface tones; duplicated specimens; any floating debris. Single specimen only, clearly dominant in the frame. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars, instrument data bars or watermarks anywhere in the image.

Square 1:1, 1080x1080.

PAPER RULE (most important): the warm, softly mottled AGED PAPER is the background and it must FILL THE ENTIRE FRAME, edge to edge and corner to corner, with its grain and foxing running right off all four sides. Do NOT paint the artwork as a separate sheet, card or page lying on a table, desk or any surface. NO mat, NO border, NO frame, NO drop shadow, NO torn or deckled paper edge, NO grey or dark panel around a sheet, NO vignette, NO letterbox bars.

SUBJECT (the most important instruction): a single, long, UNBRANCHED, cylindrical fibre, large and diagonal across the composition, painted in rich translucent washes with fine ink linework for the outlines, cropped by the frame edge at BOTH ends so its great length reads clearly — it never forks into a Y, tapers into a branch, and never sits as a short segment fully contained inside the frame. Painted a PALE PINK-CREAM wash throughout (never deep red, never grey), and clearly the widest, largest-diameter fibre of its kind, with a soft darker wash halo laid directly on the paper behind it.

Both patterns are visible at once — the transverse ladder-rung bands crossing the fibre, and the fine lengthwise myofibril grain inside each band — the way woven fabric shows both a weft and a warp.

Muted botanical-plate palette: pale pink-cream, dusty rose, cream, ochre, golden-tan, soft slate blue and violet, on warm cream paper.
